summary: This run expanded the competitor set from a few proof points into a real market map. Currency.Wiki is the biggest direct commercial benchmark. Click Currency remains the clearest proof that monetization is possible but weak ratings make it a warning, not a model. Shopping assistants like BestPrice Assistant and Savely matter because they monetize the same user intent more directly.

notable_changes.change: Verified current Chrome listing at 384 users and 22 ratings with a 2.0 rating while the official site still pushes a lifetime premium upsell.
Verified public pricing details this run: 799 USD/year lite, 1799 USD/year intermediate, 4499 USD/year prime.
FX Inline public marketplace metadata remains inconsistent with the repo version, which worsens competitive trust.

newly_relevant_products_or_launches.why_it_matters: Fresh Reddit launch activity on 2026-04-16 and 2026-04-17 shows new entrants still see this category as open enough to attack.

competitors_reviewed.traction: 60,000 users and 4.8 rating from Chrome store snippet
competitors_reviewed.pricing_model: Freemium with 7.95 USD/month Extension Pro and paid credit packs
competitors_reviewed.why_it_matters: Best current proof that browser-based currency conversion can be monetized seriously.
Large incumbent with middling ratings proves feature depth alone does not create love.
Reviews reveal the setup, performance, and accuracy problems that buyers punish.
Strong browsing-centric controls create ideas worth copying, but settings friction is a warning.
Monetization proof plus a warning that weak quality and trust poison monetization.
Shows that 'save time and money while shopping' is a stronger mainstream message than raw currency conversion.
Affiliate and savings-led positioning competes for the same shopper intent.
Validates B2B willingness to pay for currency-related infrastructure.

competitors_reviewed.traction: Global brand with active partner programs
competitors_reviewed.why_it_matters: Validates creator and affiliate monetization if traffic ever exists.
Validates travel-intent monetization, but also highlights how far FX Inline is from having a traffic engine.
